newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LEWIS BLASTS SURREY TO THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LEWIS BLASTS SURREY TO THE TOP.

text.p: England discard Chris Lewis lashed 63 off 47 deliveries to set up Surrey for a thrilling last-ball victory which put them top of the Sunday League.
Surrey beat Northamptonshire by two wickets at The Oval to lead the 40 overs competition from Nottinghamshire on run rate, both teams having won 11 of 16 matches for 46 points.

Lewis, dropped by England from the recent one-day series against Pakistan after arriving late during the third and final test, captured the spotlight from fellow all-rounder David Capel, who struck a superb 112.
Capel's innings contained two sixes and 11 fours and powered Northants to 234 for nine, while England newcomer Adam Hollioake finished with five for 58.

Surrey slipped to 100 for five, then Lewis and Nadeem Shahid (41) cracked 59 off 44 balls to lead a revival that culminated in paceman Martin Bicknell, with two needed off the last ball, smashing it to the boundary.
Lewis's former county Nottinghamshire kept firmly in the title race after an emphatic six-wicket win over Leicestershire at Trent Bridge in a rain-hit game.
Notts were set a target of 195 in 33 overs but skipper Paul Johnson blasted three sixes and six fours in an unbeaten 85 off just 61 deliveries as they won with 16 balls to spare.

Yorkshire, who were not involved in the current round of games, are two points behind the leaders in third place, with Somerset moving up to fourth, four points off the pace, after beating Derbyshire by 12 runs at Taunton.
Derbyshire, pursuing a target of 222, were spurred by Australian Dean Jones' 81 off 104 balls, only to collapse from 152 for one to 209 for eight.
